newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dow rise boosts German shares boosted in late IBIS.
newsitem.headline: Dow rise boosts German shares boosted in late IBIS.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares, now including newly-floated Deutsche Telekom, was boosted in late computerised trade on Tuesday as Wall Street opened higher.
But dealers said if it had not been for the losses of shares in new member Telekom, the index could have reached new record levels above 2,800 points.
The IBIS DAX, measuring electronic trade in the DAX index, was up 12.89 points, or 0.47 percent, at 2,781.79, well above the bourse closing level of 2,764.09 points.
Telekom shares, which traded for the first time on Monday in Europe's biggest initial public offering, ended bourse dealings down over five percent, or 1.83 marks at 32.07 marks.

In post-bourse dealing, specially extended by two hours to accomodate high trading volumes in Telekom shares, the stock slid below a technical support level of 32 marks to hit a low of 31.65 marks, before recovering somewhat to 31.90 marks by 1714 GMT.
But even this level was still well above the issue price of 28.50 marks.
Dealers said players were taking profit in both Frankfurt and New York, where the stock also opened lower.
"Big and small investors are cashing in," said one trader.

Volumes in the market debutante were greater than a normal day's trading in all the DAX 30 shares combined, with over 11 million changing hands in bourse dealings and over 20 million in computer trade.
Although most attention was still focused on Telekom, figures out at German haircare and cosmetics group Wella AG put the firm in the spotlight.
Preference shares in Wella tumbled nearly seven percent, dropping 59 marks to 810 marks in bourse dealings, after the group announced a drop in nine month group pre-tax profit.
Meanwhile, shares in German's largest bank Deutsche Bank were up 3.10 marks at 71.60 marks, recovering losses made in very thin late Monday computer dealing sparked by just one order, dealers said.
